MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  February 23, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:09 p.m., on Monday, February 23, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
ABSENT:  MAZA

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Management Analyst Alvarez

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maloney

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

MALONEY:  Mayor MALONEY briefly addressed the public and anyone who wished to speak on
federal immigration enforcement in the City of Alhambra. Mr. Maloney noted that the item was not on
the current agenda and summarized Council’s direction from the February 9, 2026 meeting. He
provided a brief update on the actions of Staff and Council since that meeting as well as actions taken
by Los Angeles County and California State Senate. He stated that Council hoped to have an
agendized discussion soon.

MAZA:  Councilmember Maza entered Council Chambers at 6:12 p.m.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS (TIME LIMITATIONS: 3 MINUTES PER
SPEAKER, 30 MINUTES TOTAL) – F2M26-4

  1) Randye KAY, 723 W. Hellman Ave., spoke against the proposed data center project in
  Monterey Park and requested Council vote on an emergency ordinance to ban the construction
  of data centers in Alhambra.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., spoke regarding federal immigration enforcement
  and corrected statements he made at the February 9th meeting regarding the number of police
  officers and Immigration Customs Enforcement officers in Milwaukee. He also noted the recent
  passing of his neighbor, a retired postal worker and long time resident of Alhambra.

  3) Melissa MICHELSON, via Zoom representing SGV Progressive Alliance, spoke against the
  proposed data center project in Monterey Park and requested an immediate moratorium on
  the construction of data centers in Alhambra. She suggested a review of Objective Design
  1
2-23-26
   Standards to help ensure City of control over what developers could build.

PUBLIC HEARING

1.  PUBLIC HEARING FOR A SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT TO THE 2025-2026 ANNUAL
  ACTION PLAN FOR THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG)
  PROGRAM – F2M25-36, N2M25-166, M2M26-33

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M25-166 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing on the proposed Substantial Amendment to the 2025-26 Annual Action Plan to receive
  public comment on the proposed changes. Management Analyst ALVAREZ delivered a staff
  report. From time to time, it is necessary for the City to process Substantial Amendments to
  allow for new or modified activities or other program-related administrative actions, as well as
  to ensure expenditure timeliness compliance. Staff sought authorization to establish a new
  infrastructure activity in the current 2025-2026 Action Plan Year in an amount up to $374,114
  from prior unspent CDBG funds. The project was an eligible CDBG activity under Section
  570.201(c) of the Federal Regulations (Public Facility and Improvements Activity), and it met
  the National Objective of benefiting Limited Clientele Activities 570.208(a)(2)(ii)(A). The
  proposed project included sidewalk, apron, curb, and gutter improvements. However, CDBG
  funds would be used specifically for the repair of approximately 21,437 square feet of sidewalk
  to improve accessibility for seniors and persons with disabilities and mobility impairments.
  This Substantial Amendment to the 2025-2026 Annual Action Plan would ensure the
  City was compliant with CDBG spending requirements under 24 CFR 570.902(a). On January
  6, 2026, staff presented the proposed project to the Housing and Community Development
  Citizen Advisory Committee (HCDA), with the HCDA in concurrence with staff’s
  recommendation to proceed to the public hearing. The Substantial Amendment was published
  in the local newspaper (Pasadena Star News), and made available for review at City Hall, the
  Alhambra Library, and the City’s CDBG administration website. The 30-day review period
  began on January 23, 2026 and concluded on February 23, 2026 at 5:00 PM. No comments
  were received as of the drafting of the staff report. The complete Substantial Amendment to
  the City of Alhambra 2025-2026 Annual Action Plan can be found here:
  https://www.alhambraca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/7409/Substantial-Amendment-to-the-
  2025-2026-Action-Plan?bidId=

  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. ALVAREZ discussed the map included in the staff
  report which showed locations of improvements in the City, and discussed the areas of high
  need throughout the City. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER requested staff provide specific data as
  to equitable distribution of improvements in each district in order to respond to the greatest
  need.

  Opened Public Hearing:  Mayor Maloney opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., representing the HCDA
  Committee, spoke regarding the HCDA discussion of the Substantial Amendment and stated
  that the Committee was unanimous in their support of the Substantial Amendment.

  Closed Public Hearing:  After receiving public comment, Mayor Maloney closed the
  public hearing.

  Discussion: Mayor MALONEY discussed the map included with the staff report which
  showed the locations of improvements in the City and supported the Substantial Amendment.
  Councilmember LEE and Mr. ALVAREZ discussed the sidewalk improvement projects and the
  public works assessment which detailed the highest priority locations. City Manager
  2
2-23-26
   BINNQUIST and Ms. LEE discussed projects of previous years such as ADA ramp
  improvements. Ms. LEE went on to discuss more equitable assessment of public works
  projects for each district. Councilmember WANG and Mr. ALVAREZ discussed the funding
  allocation. Ms. WANG agreed with Council comments regarding an equitable assessment of
  needs and also discussed staff’s metrics for determining the highest priority projects. Mr.
  MALONEY supported the Substantial Amendment based on the map provided. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER suggested Council further review and discuss topics of equity during
  the next Strategic Planning Session.

  Action Taken: City Council:

  1.  Opened the public hearing and receive public comment;
  2.  Closed the public hearing and at the City Council’s discretion, approved a Substantial
  Amendment to the 2025-2026 Annual Action Plan to establish a new public
  infrastructure project in the amount up to $374,114 from unspent prior year CDBG
  funds;
  3.  Appropriated revenue and expenditure funds in the amount of $374,114 for the 2025
  CDBG Sidewalk Improvement Project; and,
  4.  Directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-
  33)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, WANG, MAZA, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

2.  2025 CITY ACCOMPLISHMENTS REPORT – F2M25-28

  Deputy City Manager HEMBREE delivered the presentation which is on file in the City Clerk’s
  office. Staff outlined the 2025 Accomplishments Report which highlighted many of the past
  year’s achievements. The accomplishments aligned with the City’s Strategic Plan, which is
  prioritized to reflect the community’s core values. The Report was intended to heighten
  community awareness of new and ongoing activities and projects.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE asked a question regarding the Library serving as a
  Federal FEMA assistance site after the Eaton Canyon wildfires and staff provided clarification.
  She also asked a question regarding the Police Homeless Outreach Mental Evaluation
  (HOME) Team members and Ms. HEMBREE provided clarification. Council each thanked staff
  for their work.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

3.  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 AND RESOLUTION
  ADOPTING FY 2025-26 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS – F2M25-17, R2M26-4

  Director of Finance LIEU delivered a staff report and presentation, which is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office. On June 23, 2025, the City Council adopted the two-year budget for Fiscal Years
  2025-26 and 2026-27. Staff presented the Mid-Year Budget Review to provide an update on
  the Fiscal Year 2025-26 budget. During the fiscal year, unforeseen financial needs and
  opportunities typically arise, which require City Council approval of recommended adjustments
  3
2-23-26
   to projected revenues and expenditures. Staff presented a mid-year Budget review to provide
  a Budget update for FY 2025-26. The Director of Finance provided the City Council will a high-
  level overview of audited actual results for Fiscal Year 2024-25 and updated budget
  projections for Fiscal Year 2025-26. Staff also requested that the City Council approve a
  resolution adopting the FY 2025-26 Budget adjustments.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the Inclusionary
  Housing Trust Fund. Mr. McCammon distributed handouts to Council related to the in-lieu
  field study and discussed them, copies of which handouts are on file in the City Clerk’s Office.

  Mayor MALONEY and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the other updates to the Alhambra
  Municipal Code, as referenced by Mr. McCammon.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER thanked staff for their work. Councilmember
  WANG and Ms. LIEU discussed the decrease in sales revenue. Ms. WANG continued to
  discuss the decrease and requested staff review the trends and present options for a “trigger-
  point” to turn to a more conservative budget. Ms. LIEU provided clarifications. Councilmember
  MAZA echoed previous comments and supported Ms. Lieu’s comments regarding a review of
  economic trends. Councilmember LEE also discussed the decrease in sales tax and the
  Strategic Plan goal of the “Shop Local” program as a means to increase sales tax. Ms.
  BINNQUIST provided clarification regarding Strategic Plan sessions. Ms. LEE and Ms. LIEU
  discussed the increase in automobile accidents and the effect on the City budget. Mayor
  MALONEY further discussed the increase in automobile accidents. He went on to discuss the
  non-general funds with Ms. LIEU. He also discussed the decrease in sales tax revenue.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the Mid-Year Budget Review and
  related reports; and, adopted Resolution No. R2M26-4 entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra
  City Council adopting Fiscal Year 2025-26 Budget Adjustments of the City of Alhambra, Golf
  Course Clubhouse Corporation, Alhambra Capital Improvements Corporation, Alhambra
  Parking Authority, Alhambra Facilities Financing Authority And The Alhambra Public Financing
  Authority

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  ADOPT A RESOLUTION MODIFYING RESOLUTION NO. R2M24-13 APPROVING
  VARIOUS CITY FEES AND SERVICE CHARGES – F2M24-39, R2M26-3, M2M26-40

  Director of Finance LIEU delivered a staff report. Resolution No. R2M24-13 would establish
  the City’s Comprehensive Fee and Service Charge Schedule, which has historically been
  adjusted based on changes in the Consumer Price Index. During the normal course of
  operations, staff identified certain services with recoverable costs that were not included in the
  existing fee schedule. A fee study was conducted to evaluate these services and determine
  appropriate cost recovery levels. The recommended fees were presented for City Council
  consideration and proposed inclusion in the Comprehensive Fee and Service Charge
  Schedule. Staff recommended adoption of the revised fees as outlined in the February 23,
  2026 staff report by the Director of Finance.

  Public Comment:  Tom FERGUSON, 106 S. Chapel Ave., stated that the fees for appeals
  to the Planning Commission were too high and requested that the fees be lowered.

  4
2-23-26
   Discussion: Councilmember LEE agreed with Mr. Ferguson’s comments regarding the fees
  for appeals to the Planning Commission and stated that they should not be deterrents to
  residents who wished to appeal a Planning Commission approval. She requested Council
  consider lowering fees and stated that she would discuss the matter further during Item 5. Vice
  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the short-term rental
  permit fees. Councilmember WANG, Ms. LIEU and Director of Community Development HO
  discussed the vacant storefront fees. Ms. WANG requested more information regarding the
  impact on businesses. Councilmember MAZA and Mr. HO discussed the mobile food vending
  fees.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M26-3 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council modifying Resolution No. R2M24-13 approving various city fees
  and service charges; and, directed the Finance Director to make the necessary budget
  adjustments for the approved fee and service charge charges. (M2M26-40)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  COUNCIL DISCUSSION CONCERNING HEALTH AND SAFETY STANDARDS FOR
  CERTAIN HOUSING PROJECTS, AUTOMATIC APPEALS OF SAME RETROACTIVE TO
  DECEMBER 1, 2025, AND DISPLACED TENANT ASSISTANCE – F2M26-7

  City Attorney MONTES delivered a staff report. At the January 26, 2026 Council Meeting and
  then again at the February 9, 2026 City Council Meeting, Councilmember Lee requested that
  the Council agendize a discussion concerning two matters: 1.) Establishing health and safety
  standards for certain multi-story, multi-family housing projects to better regulate those projects
  in proximity to single family residential properties; and, 2.) Requiring automatic appeals of
  multi-family housing projects where objections concerning health and safety are made during
  the approval process, retroactive to December 1, 2025. A majority of the Council concurred in
  the request, with Mayor Maloney requesting that the topic of tenant assistance for those
  displaced by new housing projects also be discussed. The Council concurred in the addition
  of this topic. The City Attorney and Director of Community Development will provide some
  legal context to assist in the Council’s discussion as it pertains to the following: 1.) Health and
  Safety Standards for multi-family housing; 2.) Automatic appeals of certain multifamily housing
  projects retroactive to December 1, 2025; and, 3.) Tenant Relocation Assistance.

  Public Comment:

  1) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the project at 110 S. Chapel Ave. and
  requested help for people being evicted at no fault of their own. He also distributed
  handouts, which are on file in the City Clerk’s office. He discussed housing assistance and
  the need for more affordable housing units.

  2)  Holly PENDERGAST, 110 S. Chapel Ave., spoke against the project at 110 S. Chapel
  Ave. as a resident that was being evicted at no fault of her own and requested financial
  assistance. She requested conditions be applied to minimize the impact of the effects on
  neighbors. She also distributed handouts, which are on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  3) Stephen HOLMAN, 106 S. Chapel Ave., spoke against the project at 110 S. Chapel Ave.
  and spoke in support of a retroactive appeal of the project.

  5
2-23-26
   4) Thomas FERGUSON, 106 S. Chapel Ave., read a letter he submitted to Council and which
  is on file in the City Clerk’s office. The letter was against the project at 110 S. Chapel Ave.
  and in support of a retroactive appeal of the project.

  5) Alborz MOHTASHAMI, 1621 S. Monterey St., spoke against the implementation of sub-
  items 1 and 2 as violations of State law, and requested staff prepare more information
  regarding sub-item 3.

  6) Elliott LEE, via Zoom, spoke against the implementation of items 1 and 2 as violations of
  State law and threats to the Housing Element.

  7) Melissa MICHELSON, via Zoom, spoke in favor of the items and urged Council to act in
  favor of the health and safety of residents.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE discussed the project, expressed sympathy for the
  displaced tenants, and motioned that $3,000 per household tenant be paid directly to the
  landlord as relocation assistance. Ms. LEE, Director of Community Development HO, and Mr.
  MONTES discussed sub-item 1, objective standards in terms of health and safety. Ms. LEE
  went on to discuss the need to study the impact of the project on surrounding neighborhood
  in terms of air quality, water quality, sunlight exposure, and noise exposure. Mr. MONTES
  provided clarification regarding objective standards, restrictions which would limit the intensity
  of the land use and therefore require approval from HCD. They continued the discussion.

  Ms. LEE proposed that the developer submit a shade study for the existing property and a
  projected study for the proposed project. She stated that if the study showed a decrease of at
  least 50% on neighboring properties, then this would pose a health concern. Ms. LEE
  suggested standards regarding air pollution during construction as well as a projected impact
  from the cars of new residents. Mr. MONTES provided clarification regarding the project’s
  exemption from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) studies. She motioned that
  the shade study requirement be included as an objective standard.

  Ms. LEE went on to speak in support of sub-item 2 regarding an automatic appeal of the
  project. She proposed that once a project has been approved, that information be mailed to
  affected neighbors allowing them to submit rationale in favor of an automatic appeal to the
  project. She stated that there should not be any fees associated with this. She stated that staff
  would review the submitted rationales and determine if an appeal would go before Council.
  She motioned that the automatic appeal process be implemented. She stated that all three
  points be included in her motion.

  Councilmember MAZA expressed sympathy for the displaced residents, spoke to the
  responsibility of Council to follow State law, discussed the Housing Element, stated that he
  was not in favor of sub-items 1 and 2, and supported further discussion of Item 3. He continued
  to discuss use of Inclusionary Housing funds and the administration of such funds. He
  encouraged staff to look into the unauthorized demolition mentioned by Mr. Holman. Mr. MAZA
  and Mr. FERGUSON discussed the involvement of Code Enforcement and communication
  with staff.

  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER expressed sympathy for the displaced residents. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER and Director of Community Development discussed the City’s Housing
  Element and Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) allocations in terms of this project.
  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER also discussed the difficulties of housing development in the City.
  She discussed the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance and in-lieu fees with Mr. HO. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. MONTES discussed shade studies as part of objective
  standards. They went on to discuss the City’s certified Housing Element, and the negative
  6
2-23-26
   impact on the City if HCD determines that the City has violated it. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  stated that she supported further discussion of sub-item 3 for Displaced Tenant Assistance.
  She requested an agendized discussion.

  Mr. MAZA, Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER, and Mr. HO discussed the developer including 10%
  affordable units for Low and Very Low-Income Households. Mr. MONTES provided
  clarification. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER emphasized staff review the Inclusionary Housing In-
  Lieu fund to provide tenant assistance.

  Councilmember WANG expressed sympathy for the displaced residents. She went on to
  further discuss the City’s RHNA obligation. Ms. WANG and Mr. HO discussed the impact of
  using the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance and Inclusionary In-Lieu Fee fund guidelines for
  tenant relocation funds on the City’s RHNA allocation, despite not one of the approved or
  intended uses. Ms. WANG continued to discuss the City’s RHNA obligation. With regards to
  sub-item 3 and Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s suggestion, Ms. WANG further suggested staff explore
  options for developers to contribute to the tenant relocation assistance rather than use the
  Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu fee fund, as it would be an unintended use of fees.

  Ms. WANG went on to discuss sub-item 2 and the discussion at the Planning Commission
  meetings. She discussed the restrictions of State law and the arguments against denying the
  project which were thoroughly discussed by Planning Commission. Ms. WANG and Mr.
  MONTES discussed sub-item 1 in terms of the applicability of Council approved health and
  safety standards on the approved project, the potential legal challenges to standards which
  could limit the intensity of use on a site, and the impact on the Housing Element.

  Mayor MALONEY supported continued discussion on tenant relocation assistance and went
  on to discuss the needs of the community that are not being met through new developments,
  the Inclusionary Housing fund, and tenants who have been evicted through no-fault of their
  own. He did not support sub-items 1 and 2 due to the fact that there would not be a legal path
  to pursue them. He continued to discuss points made by Mr. Montes, Mr. Maza, Ms. Andrade-
  Stadler, and Ms. Wang. He also continued to discuss issues of RHNA, the Housing Element,
  the housing crisis in California, and the displacement of residents through development. He
  suggested Council direct staff to return with a report regarding tenant relocation assistance
  and potential actions to address the concerns of residents displaced by the project at 110 S.
  Chapel Ave as well as any future displaced tenants.

  Council continued to discuss the item and the sub-items 1, 2, and 3. Ms. LEE continued to
  support and discuss points related to her motion to 1) update the Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu
  fund to include tenant relocation assistance which would be provided to low-moderate income
  residents displaced by new developments beginning in December 1, 2025 in the amount of
  $3,000 per household to be directly paid to the new landlord; 2) direct staff to develop Health
  and Safety Standards to include sun shade studies on proposed developments which would
  be applied during approval and appeal process; 3) grant automatic appeals to the City Council
  of Certain Housing Projects Retroactive to December 1, 2025. Council discussed Ms. Lee’s
  comments and Mr. MONTES provided clarification.

  Mr. MALONEY made a substitute motion to direct staff to look into tenant relocation assistance
  as it applies to tenants in question related to the development at 110 S. Chapel Ave. and future
  tenants in similar situations. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER requested an amendment to the
  motion for staff to look into the Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu fund as a potential funding source
  as well as Measure A funds which could be used to prevent homelessness. Mr. MALONEY
  accepted the addition to the motion from Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER seconded the substitute motion.

  7
2-23-26
   Action Taken:  City Council discussed and provided direction to City staff to look into
  displaced tenant relocation assistance, as it applies to tenants in question related to the
  development at 110 S. Chapel Ave. and future tenants in similar situations.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 20): (TIME LIMITATIONS: 5 MINUTES PER SPEAKER FOR
ONE ITEM, 10 MINUTES PER SPEAKER FOR 2+ ITEMS)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine and were
enacted by one motion.

6.  AWARD CONTRACT: WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON SEVENTH STREET
  BETWEEN VALLEY BOULEVARD AND SHORB STREET – F2M25-63, N2M25-174,
  C2M26-12, M2M26-30

  On December 8, 2025, the City Council approved the distribution of Notice Inviting Bids for the
  Water Main Replacement Seventh Street from Valley Boulevard to Shorb Street. On February
  5, 2026, bids were opened by the City Clerk. Five bids were received, which ranged from
  amount of $444,760.00 to the high bid of $726,250. Ramona Inc. submitted the lowest qualified
  bid at $444,760.00. Staff reviewed the bid submitted by Ramona Inc., and found it to be in full
  compliance and conformance with the project’s specifications.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and Ramona Inc.
  for the Water Main Replacement on Seventh Street from Valley Boulevard to Shorb Street in
  an amount not to exceed $444,760.00; determined that the Water Main Replacement Seventh
  Street from Valley Boulevard to Shorb Street Project is categorically exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 (b); and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M26-30)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AWARD CONTRACT: POPLAR BOULEVARD REHABILITATION PROJECT (STPL-
  5130(024)) – F2M25-55, N2M25-145, C2M26-13, M2M26-31

  The Notice Inviting Bids for the Poplar Boulevard Rehabilitation Project was approved for
  distribution by the City Council on October 13, 2025. On December 4, 2025, the City Clerk
  received eight bids that ranged from $673,956.00 to $1,098,496.00. Staff reviewed the bids
  and found the one received from Gentry Brothers, Inc. in the amount of $673,956 to be the
  lowest responsible bid. Gentry Brothers, Inc. had the necessary licenses to complete the work
  and has completed similar projects for the City of Alhambra.

  Discussion:  None
  8
2-23-26
   Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Gentry Brothers, Inc. in the amount of $673,956.00 for
  the Poplar Boulevard Rehabilitation Project (HSIP-5130(024)); and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M26-31)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: GOLF  COURSE  PARKING  AREA  LANDSCAPE
  ENHANCEMENT PROJECT – F2M25-46, C2M25-43, M2M26-32

  On October 13, 2025, the City Council awarded a contract to Four Seasons Landscaping Inc.
  in the amount of $109,000 for the Golf Course Parking Area Landscape Enhancement project.
  The City requested a change order to remove the old dying trees in the landscaping area which
  totaled $16,000, which brings the contract total to $125,000. This project was inspected by
  staff, and all work was completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and
  specifications. As such, it would be appropriate for the City Council to accept this project as
  complete.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of SGD Enterprises DBA Four Seasons
  Landscaping, Inc. for the Alhambra Golf Course Parking Area Landscape Enhancement
  Project as complete in the amount of $125,000.00; directed the City Clerk to file a Notice of
  Completion with the County of Los Angeles for recordation; instructed the Finance Director to
  release the 5% retention 35 days from the date of recordation if no liens and filed; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-32)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: 2024 CDBG ADA RAMP PROJECT – F2M25-26, C2M25-17,
  M2M26-34

  On April 28, 2025, the City Council awarded a contract to CJ Concrete, Inc. for the 2024
  CDBG ADA Ramp Project in the amount of $638,125.00. One change order was issued
  resulting in an increase of $21,193.50 for an additional ramp, making the final cost
  $659,318.50. The project was inspected by staff and all work was completed in accordance
  with the City’s requirements and specifications. As such, it would be appropriate for the City
  Council to accept this project as complete and instruct that the Notice of Completion be filed
  with the County of Los Angeles Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of CJ Concrete Construction, Inc. for
  the 2024 CDBG ADA Ramp Project as complete in the amount of $659,318.50; directed the
  City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with the County of Los Angeles for recordation;
  9
2-23-26

20.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING THE PRIMA FACIE
  SPEED LIMITS IN SCHOOL ZONES IN THE CITY – F2M26-7, O2M26-4857

  Staff requested that the City Council consider second reading and adoption of an ordinance
  adding Section 11.08.075 to Chapter 11.08 of the Alhambra Municipal Code establishing a
  prima facia speed limit of 20 miles per hour in school zones. The recent passage of AB 382
  enabled cities to reduce the speed limit in school zones to 20 miles per hour when children
  are present. A school zone is defined as an area of 500 feet in all directions on the roads
  adjoining a school. At the January 12, 2026 City Council meeting, Councilwoman Adele
  Andrade-Stadler requested that an item be agendized setting a speed limit of 20 miles per
  hour for the Council’s consideration. The City Council concurred in the request. The proposed
  ordinance would establish a prima facia speed limit of 20 miles per hour in school zones when
  children are present, with the posting of appropriate signage to that effect. The proposed
  ordinance was given first reading at the February 9, 2026 City Council meeting.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its second reading and adopt the
  following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M26-4857: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council
  adding Section 11.08.075 to Chapter 11.08 of the Alhambra Municipal Code
  establishing a prima facia speed limit of 20 miles per hour in school zones
